text:
For once, the Flyers made the play late. Denver Barkey's second goal of the night, 11:54 into the third, broke a 3-3 tie in Columbus and held up, and it was the first time all season Philadelphia had won a game that was tied at any point in the third period, as PHLY's Charlie O'Connor pointed out. After a week spent arguing about Matvei Michkov, the young winger was in the middle of it too.

It started badly. Dmitri Voronkov scored 3:19 in on a shot that goes in about 3% of the time, and Matthew Knies made it 2-0 a minute later. Trevor Zegras got one back late in the first, set up on the doorstep by Tyson Foerster. Then the Flyers had their best two minutes of the week: Michkov went end to end on his own for a backhand at 1:19 of the second, which O'Connor called "an absolutely fantastic individual effort", and Barkey scored on the power play 62 seconds later. Adam Fantilli tied it three minutes after that, and Columbus was the better team for the rest of the period, out-chancing Philadelphia 1.66 expected goals to 0.77.

Barkey's winner, set up by Noel Acciari, moved Philadelphia's win chance from 48% to 82%, and Joseph Woll made it stand, stopping Kent Johnson in the final minutes. Woll made 28 saves on 31 shots, about what those shots deserved. At the other end Jet Greaves allowed four on 21, two more than the shots usually produce.

The honest reading is that the Flyers stole one. Columbus had 66 shot attempts to 43 and won this game in 68% of our replays. O'Connor also noted Rick Tocchet swapping a defenseman onto a late power play, which he sees as part of a team that plays it safe close and late. The Blue Jackets, without Conor Garland and Sean Monahan, are winless in four. Philadelphia goes home to face Edmonton tonight.
headline: Barkey and Michkov give the Flyers a late win, finally
